# Workflow Conventions

## CI/release workflow separation

CI (build/test) and release (publish/tag) are separate workflows:

- **`placeframe-ci.yml`**: Triggers on `push: [dev]` and `pull_request: [dev]`. Contains: preflight, unity (calls `unity-build.yml`), build-docker, publish-compose, ensure-release-pr. The `ensure-release-pr` job is gated on all builds passing and only runs on dev push.
- **`unity-build.yml`**: lives in the [unity-devkit](https://github.com/outernet-foundation/unity-devkit) repo (moved there by the tooling-consolidation program); the Unity jobs (matrix, activate-license, build-unity) run from placeframe-ci as a cross-repo `workflow_call` pinned to a pushed SHA, `secrets: inherit`. The workflow is self-contained by contract — no relative composite-action references (those resolve against the *caller's* checkout), no repo-specific values — and that contract is maintained in unity-devkit now; placeframe projects participate through their `unity-build.json` manifests and `ProjectVersion.txt` (editor images are matrix-emitted), never through workflow edits. Changes to the hosted workflow land on unity-devkit's own CI and reach placeframe through deliberate SHA bumps — placeframe PRs exercise the pinned copy, not a local file. The caller's `unity` job is deliberately ungated — Unity builds run parallel to preflight for faster PR feedback; release gating is enforced by `ensure-release-pr`'s `needs` instead.
- **`placeframe-release.yml`**: Triggers on `push: [main]`, `workflow_dispatch`, and on the Placeframe workflow completing green on `dev` (`workflow_run`). The `release` job (main pushes + non-dev dispatch) reuses CI artifacts by looking up the successful CI run for the same SHA via `gh api`. The `publish-dev` job (green dev pushes, or a dispatch with `dev-publish=true` + `dev-run-id` against `dev`) runs pubpkg's `publish-dev`: immutable `-dev.<ci-run-id>` prereleases of every path-diff-changed package, keyed by the CI run that proved greenness — no git tags, npm `latest` untouched, and the printed versions are the consumption interface (exact pins by hand). Dispatch matters because `workflow_run` triggers only register from the workflow file on the **default branch**: until the release merge lands this file on `main`, the dev channel is armed solely by dispatching against `dev` (a dispatch runs the dispatched ref's copy of the file). The dev jobs live in this workflow file — not in placeframe-ci — because npm allows one trusted publisher per package, bound to a single workflow filename that must be shared with the stable publish jobs. PyPI packages are split out of both flows into per-package matrix jobs (`release-pypi`, `publish-dev-pypi`), each entry under its own `pypi-<project>` GitHub environment: PyPI trusted publishers are identified by `(owner, repo, workflow filename, environment)` with one project per tuple, so multi-package repos need one environment per PyPI package. The main jobs exclude the PyPI pair; the stable main job keeps app-version handling (`--with-apps`) and the matrix runs before `release` so `create-release` sees every tag. Uses `cancel-in-progress: false` — never abort a publish mid-flight, and the shared `release` concurrency group serializes dev publishes against stable releases.
- All workflow logic lives in Python scripts invoked via `uv run` — no inline shell conditionals or loops (per repo-root convention).
